value:
The SaunaLife Model G6 is a factory-assembled outdoor sauna cabin built with a furniture-grade alder interior, painted spruce exterior, full tempered-glass front wall, LED lighting, and Bluetooth audio. It removes the cabin-building work from a backyard sauna project — but you still need a level raised foundation, heavy-equipment offloading, a separately purchased heater, and certified electrical installation (SaunaLife, 2025; SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024; SaunaHeaters, n.d.).

TL;DR

  • Arrives built, not ready to run. The cabin ships assembled inside a protective OSB box; final assembly, placement, and hookup happen on site (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024).

  • Plan for weight. The manual lists the sauna at 2,645 lbs, and 2,976 lbs boxed. Offloading generally requires a forklift or crane (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024).

  • The heater is sold separately. Budget for the heater, its controls, and the labor to install both (SaunaHeaters, n.d.).

  • Two electrical systems. The manual documents a 240 VAC cabinet for heater controls and ventilation and a 120 VAC cabinet for lighting, with heater-side wiring supporting up to 11 kW / 46 A. All connections require a certified electrician (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024).

  • Foundation rule to memorize: stable, level, and at least 3 inches above the surrounding ground (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024).

  • Capacity language is inconsistent. It is commonly marketed as a five-person sauna, while official materials also reference up to six bathers (GoOutdoorDirect, 2025; SaunaLife, 2025).

What the SaunaLife Model G6 Actually Is

Definition box

Pre-assembled outdoor sauna: A sauna delivered as a completed cabin rather than a flat-pack kit. It reduces on-site construction but still requires site preparation, placement, heater installation, and electrical work (SaunaLife, 2025; SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024).

SaunaLife Model G6: A premium outdoor sauna cabin in SaunaLife's Garden Series, built with a furniture-grade alder interior, painted spruce exterior, glass-front design, and integrated lighting and audio (SaunaLife, 2025).

Key terms and thresholds

Term

What it means for you

Alder interior

A sauna-friendly hardwood chosen for its smoother feel and lower surface heat, which makes benches more comfortable against skin (SaunaLife, 2025)

Painted spruce exterior

A common outdoor sauna cladding, suited to weather exposure but not maintenance-free (SaunaLife, 2025)

Double-glazed tempered glass

Two panes with an air gap, tempered for strength and safer breakage behavior (SaunaLife, 2025)

IP67 rating

Dust-tight and able to withstand temporary immersion under defined test conditions — here it signals outdoor-rated electrical hardware (SaunaLife, 2025)

Two-tier benches

Seating at two heights, letting bathers choose hotter upper or cooler lower positions (SaunaMarketplace, 2026)

11 kW / 46 A

The heater-side wiring capacity documented in the manual — a ceiling, not a recommendation (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

3 inches above grade

The minimum foundation elevation stated in the manual (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

If the footprint and configuration are what you're weighing right now, it's worth reviewing the current SaunaLife Model G6 outdoor sauna package before you plan a foundation.

Experience Unrivaled Luxury and Design

Bottom line: the G6's premium position rests on verifiable materials and finish work, not on measured performance advantages.

Alder Interior, Spruce Exterior, and Glass-Front Design

The cabin pairs a furniture-grade alder interior with a painted spruce exterior, and the front wall is full tempered glass with a clear glass door (SaunaLife, 2025). That combination is what produces the architectural look in product photography — a glass face that reads as a garden structure rather than a shed.

  • Alder inside for a smoother, cooler-feeling bench surface (SaunaLife, 2025)

  • Painted spruce outside for weather-facing cladding (SaunaLife, 2025)

  • Full tempered-glass front wall and clear glass door (SaunaLife, 2025)

Evidence strength: Strong for the material specifications; Mixed for the word "luxury," which is a design and market category rather than a performance rating.

Caveat: Glass specifications here are product-oriented. Treat durability, heat retention, and efficiency comparisons as unverified unless a manufacturer publishes comparative testing.

Integrated Lighting and Audio

Lighting is dimmable LED with app or remote control, and the outdoor electrical enclosures are IP67 rated (SaunaLife, 2025). The manual confirms lighting, speakers, and the ventilator arrive prewired (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024).

  • Dimmable LED lighting, prewired at the factory (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Remote or app-based control depending on the installed control-system version (SaunaLife, 2025)

  • Bluetooth speakers with setup instructions in the manual (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • IP67-rated outdoor electrical enclosures (SaunaLife, 2025)

Evidence strength: Strong for the presence of these features; Limited on the specifics of app functionality, which may vary by control system. Confirm exact control behavior for your configuration before you assume a particular app experience.

Key Features for a Superior Sauna Experience

Bottom line: the defining feature is factory assembly. Everything else is a finish or convenience layer on top of that.

G6 Features at a Glance

  • Factory-assembled cabin, delivered built rather than flat-packed (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Two-tier bench layout (SaunaMarketplace, 2026)

  • Furniture-grade alder interior, painted spruce exterior (SaunaLife, 2025)

  • Full tempered-glass front wall and clear glass door (SaunaLife, 2025)

  • Insulated wall construction, listed by a retailer at roughly 7-1/16 in. thick (SaunaHeaters, n.d.)

  • Prewired LED lighting, Bluetooth speakers, and ventilator (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • IP67-rated outdoor electrical boxes (SaunaLife, 2025)

  • Rainwater management built into the roof drainage design (SaunaLife, 2025)

  • Heater selected and purchased separately (SaunaHeaters, n.d.)

What "Fully Assembled" Actually Means

Think prefab structure, not countertop appliance. The cabin arrives built, which eliminates the carpentry — but it does not eliminate the project.

Still required on your end:

  • A prepared, level, elevated foundation (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Delivery access wide and clear enough for freight and lifting equipment (SaunaHeaters, n.d.)

  • Forklift or crane offloading (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Final placement and on-site assembly steps (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • A compatible heater (SaunaHeaters, n.d.)

  • Certified electrical installation (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

Evidence strength: Strong. Both the manufacturer's manual and retailer delivery notes support each item.

Five-Person or Six-Person Capacity?

Retail listings commonly describe the G6 as a five-person sauna (GoOutdoorDirect, 2025), while official materials also reference up to six bathers (SaunaLife, 2025). Both numbers circulate, and neither is wrong so much as differently optimistic about comfort.

  • Two-tier bench seating means usable capacity depends on how bathers distribute across upper and lower tiers (SaunaMarketplace, 2026)

  • Body size and how much personal space your household expects change the practical number

  • For planning purposes, five is the safer working assumption

Evidence strength: Mixed — this is a documented wording discrepancy between manufacturer and retail sources, not a resolved specification.

Note on the dimension figures: published measurements vary slightly between retailers, likely because of rounding, trim, or whether the measurement was taken before or after boxing (TheSaunaHeater, 2023). Manufacturer documentation should outrank retailer copy wherever the two conflict.

Weight and Shipping Footprint

The manual lists 2,645 lbs for the cabin and 2,976 lbs boxed; a retailer separately lists a 2,756 lb shipping weight (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024; SaunaHeaters, n.d.). These figures use different bases, so don't blend them — use the manual's numbers for rigging and foundation planning.

The boxed dimensions matter as much as the installed footprint. A cabin that fits beautifully in the corner of your yard is still a roughly 8-by-8-foot crate that has to travel from the truck to the pad.

What Is Included — and What Is Not

Generally part of the delivered cabin system:

  • Assembled cabin with benches and interior components

  • Prewired lighting, Bluetooth speakers, and ventilator (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Electrical and control enclosures (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

Not included, or requiring separate planning:

  • Sauna heater and, in most cases, its controls (SaunaHeaters, n.d.)

  • Professional electrical labor (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Foundation construction

  • Crane or forklift service (SaunaHeaters, n.d.)

  • Local permits

  • Any modification to the delivery path

Retailer bundles differ, so verify the current package listing before assuming what ships with your unit.

How to Do It Safely and Effectively: Installation and Setup

Bottom line: the G6 is far simpler than building a sauna, and considerably more involved than receiving an appliance. Treat it as a small construction project with a freight component.

Step 1 — Foundation

  • Build a stable, level base

  • Elevate the cabin at least 3 inches above surrounding ground (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • The manual's examples include concrete blocks or strips over compacted gravel (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • A patio or paved surface can work if the elevation and support requirements are met (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Account for drainage, local code, and soil conditions

Step 2 — Delivery and Offloading

  • The cabin ships inside a protective OSB box (SaunaHeaters, n.d.)

  • A forklift or crane is generally required to offload (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Confirm before shipment: truck access, gate width, turning radius, slope, overhead obstructions, and the full path to final placement

  • Establish in writing who is responsible for offloading. Standard freight service does not place a 2,900-pound crate on your foundation.

Step 3 — Electrical

  • The manual documents separate 120 VAC and 240 VAC systems in two enclosures behind a side door (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • 120 VAC cabinet: lighting and related components, up to 1 kW / 9 A (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • 240 VAC cabinet: heater control unit and ventilator, with heater wiring supporting up to 11 kW / 46 A (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • A certified electrician must complete all electrical connections (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Final breaker, conductor, disconnect, and control specifications must follow local code, the sauna manual, and the selected heater manufacturer's instructions

Mistakes to Avoid

  • Pouring a pad from retailer dimensions alone. Confirm the current manufacturer drawing first (TheSaunaHeater, 2023).

  • Scheduling delivery before the foundation is finished. A crated cabin has nowhere to go.

  • Assuming a single circuit covers it. There are two systems, not one (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024).

  • Buying the heater before the electrician reviews panel capacity and wire-run distance.

  • Modifying the heating system or components. The manual's warranty terms exclude coverage where misuse, alteration, commercial use, or non-approved heating changes are involved (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024).

Safety and Who Should Consult a Clinician

  • Keep the door closed during heat-up to avoid overheating the cabin (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Do not leave towels or other combustible items inside after a session (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Do not pour water over the heater when it is off (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Ventilate after each use to dry moisture and reduce mold risk (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Stay hydrated and leave the sauna if you feel unwell

  • People who are pregnant, have cardiovascular disease, take medications affecting hydration or blood pressure, or have difficulty tolerating heat should speak with a clinician before beginning routine sauna use. This is general heat-safety guidance rather than model-specific labeling.

Choosing the Right Heater for Your G6

Bottom line: start from the electrical ceiling, not the product catalog. The heater is a separate purchase and the single most consequential technical decision in the project.

Start With the Electrical Ceiling

The manual documents support for up to 11 kW / 46 A in the heater-side cabinet (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024). "Supports up to" is a wiring capacity, not a recommendation that 11 kW is the right heater for your cabin.

The heater you select must be approved for the cabin volume, the glass area, the control system, required clearances, and your property's electrical service.

The Selection Ruleset

  1. Confirm the manufacturer's current approved heater range for this model.

  2. Give your electrician the installation manual and the proposed heater specifications before anything is ordered.

  3. Verify available panel capacity and wire-run distance to the sauna location.

  4. Have the glass area and your local climate factored into the sizing review — a large glass front changes the thermal picture.

  5. Confirm control-unit and sensor compatibility, including door and temperature sensors.

  6. Confirm required safety clearances around the heater.

  7. Get written confirmation before purchasing the heater and controls.

A retailer displaying a heater next to the G6 is merchandising, not verified compatibility. Confirm the current cabin package and electrical documentation for the SaunaLife Model G6 outdoor sauna before you commit to a heater.

Placement, Floor Grid, and Airflow

  • The floor grid may need rotation or modification to accommodate heater placement and preserve airflow (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Heater placement must maintain ventilation and required clearances (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Sensor and control placement follows the heater manufacturer's instructions

  • This is installer-level work, not a styling choice.

Evidence strength: Strong for the process and the electrical boundaries; no supported basis exists in the available documentation for naming a specific heater brand or model as the correct pairing.

Where the G6 Creates Value

  • A finished alder interior and painted spruce exterior on arrival (SaunaLife, 2025)

  • A glass-front architectural design rather than a utility structure (SaunaLife, 2025)

  • Integrated lighting and audio, prewired (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • A documented outdoor installation system with published requirements (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Buyer fit: people who value a finished architectural product over maximum customization

More features do not equal better heat quality. No comparative testing in the available documentation supports that step.

G6 vs. G7 — What Can Honestly Be Said

A reliable G6-versus-G7 comparison requires current G7 specifications, and those aren't established in the sourcing behind this article. Rather than fill the gap with assumptions about capacity, footprint, materials, or heater requirements, compare configurations directly across the SaunaLife outdoor sauna collection.

Decision Framework: Is the G6 a Practical Fit?

1. Can the crated cabin physically reach the installation area? Yes → continue. No or uncertain → resolve gate width, slope, overhead clearance, turning radius, and crane reach before ordering.

2. Is a stable, level, elevated foundation ready or feasible? Yes → continue. No → price and schedule the foundation work first.

3. Can the property support separate 120 VAC and 240 VAC requirements? Yes → continue with an electrician's review. Unknown → get a panel-capacity and wire-run assessment.

4. Has a compatible heater and control package been verified in writing? Yes → continue. No → do not purchase based on wattage or retailer bundling alone.

5. Are you comfortable coordinating freight, heavy-equipment placement, and licensed electrical work? Yes → the G6 is likely a strong fit. No → consider a kit, a smaller prefab model, or a dealer-managed installation package.

Real-World Constraints and Numbers That Matter

Bottom line: the numbers that derail G6 projects are logistical, not aesthetic.

  • ~2,976 lbs boxed. This is crane or forklift territory, and it sets your foundation and rigging requirements (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024).

  • ~86 × 98 × 100 in. crated. Measure your access path against the crate, not the cabin (SaunaHeaters, n.d.).

  • 3 in. minimum elevation above grade. A non-negotiable from the manual that shapes the entire foundation design (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024).

  • Two circuits, not one. 240 VAC for heater controls and ventilation, 120 VAC for lighting (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024).

  • 11 kW / 46 A ceiling on the heater side; 1 kW / 9 A on the lighting side (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024).

  • Heater cost sits outside the cabin price, along with electrical labor, offloading, foundation work, and permits (SaunaHeaters, n.d.).

  • Warranty: the manual describes a limited lifetime warranty for qualifying residential use by the original retail purchaser, excluding heaters, added components, wear, and weathering (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024).

What is not established: operating cost per session, heat-up time under defined conditions, and comparative energy performance. Any figure you encounter for those should be traced to documented testing conditions before you build a budget on it.

Maximizing Your SaunaLife G6: Tips and Best Practices

Bottom line: an outdoor cabin is weather-resistant, not maintenance-free.

After Each Session

  • Ventilate the cabin (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Let wet surfaces dry

  • Remove towels and other moisture-holding or combustible items (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Wipe benches and cladding with a damp cloth when needed (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Avoid harsh household chemicals on wood surfaces (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Follow the heater manufacturer's instructions on water use (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

Periodic Interior Care

  • Inspect for mold or mildew (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Use a sauna-formulated wood preservative where recommended (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Check benches, fasteners, glass, seals, ventilation, and drainage

  • Do not apply unapproved coatings inside the hot room

Exterior and Seasonal Care

  • Clean the exterior annually with an appropriate outdoor wood cleaner (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Check water runoff and the rainwater drainage path (SaunaLife, 2025)

  • Inspect the exterior finish for weather exposure

  • Adjust frequency to your local climate — humid, coastal, or heavy-freeze regions will ask more of the finish than a dry one

Myths and Misconceptions

1. "Fully assembled means no installation work." The G6 still needs foundation prep, offloading, and electrical hookup (SaunaLife, 2025; SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024). Why it persists: marketing shorthand makes "assembled" sound plug-and-play.

2. "The heater comes with the sauna." The heater is sold separately (SaunaHeaters, n.d.). Why it persists: product pages center the cabin and treat heating as a later add-on.

3. "Any electrician can finish it without the manual." The manual requires a certified electrician working from both the sauna documentation and the heater manufacturer's instructions (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024). Why it persists: people underestimate the split 120/240 V arrangement.

4. "You can set it on any flat surface." The manual specifies a leveled, stable base elevated at least three inches above grade (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024). Why it persists: outdoor prefab products get mentally filed alongside patio furniture.

5. "A heavier sauna is automatically a better sauna." Weight mostly determines transport and base requirements, not the quality of the session (SaunaHeaters, n.d.). Why it persists: buyers use mass as a proxy for build quality.

6. "Glass fronts always make a sauna less efficient." The G6 uses insulated, double-glazed glass designed to perform better than single glazing (SaunaLife, 2025). Why it persists: people generalize from poorly insulated glass panels they've encountered elsewhere.

7. "The Bluetooth and LEDs are the real value." Those are convenience layers; the substance is the prefabricated cabin, materials, and build (SaunaLife, 2025; SaunaMarketplace, 2026). Why it persists: the features photograph well and lead retail listings.

8. "Outdoor means maintenance-free." The manual calls for regular ventilation, cleaning, and annual exterior care (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024). Why it persists: weather-resistant materials get read as weatherproof.

9. "It's basically a kit with a shorter build time." It isn't a kit at all — it ships as a completed cabin (SaunaLife, 2025; SaunaMarketplace, 2026). Why it persists: retailer copy blurs sauna product categories.

10. "Capacity numbers are exact." Listings conflict between five-person and up to six bathers, so capacity is approximate and depends on seating layout (GoOutdoorDirect, 2025; SaunaLife, 2025). Why it persists: different sellers assume different comfort standards.

11. "The warranty covers everything on the unit." The manual's warranty excludes heaters and added components, and can be voided by misuse, alteration, or commercial use (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024). Why it persists: "limited lifetime warranty" reads as more comprehensive than it is.

12. "Freight delivery includes placement." Offloading generally requires a forklift or crane, arranged separately (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024; SaunaHeaters, n.d.). Why it persists: most consumer deliveries end at the door, so buyers assume this one does too.

Experience Layer: A Buyer's Test Plan

No verified first-person owner logs are included here. What follows is a safe, repeatable plan you can run on your own property — before and after delivery — plus a template for recording it.

Pre-Order Site Test (do this before you buy)

  1. Mark the crate footprint. Chalk or stake roughly 86 × 98 in. on the ground where the sauna will live.

  2. Walk the delivery path from the street to that mark. Note the narrowest point, the steepest grade, and anything overhead.

  3. Measure your gate and turning radius. Compare against the crate, not the finished cabin.

  4. Photograph the electrical panel and measure the run distance to the pad.

  5. Get two quotes: one for foundation work, one for the electrical run and heater installation.

  6. Ask your dealer, in writing, who offloads and what equipment they'll bring.

Post-Delivery Observation Period (first 30 days)

What you might notice — none of this is guaranteed, and it will vary with your climate, heater, and installation:

  • Heat-up behavior differing between upper and lower bench tiers

  • The glass front changing how the space feels in daylight versus evening

  • Moisture lingering longer on some interior surfaces than others

  • Exterior finish responding to your first significant rain or freeze

  • Different comfort at different seating positions, which may change your capacity assumptions

Frequently Asked Questions

1. Is the SaunaLife G6 delivered fully assembled? Yes — it ships as a completed cabin rather than a flat-pack kit, though final assembly steps happen on site.

  • Not a kit; the cabin arrives built (SaunaLife, 2025)

  • Ships inside a protective OSB box (SaunaHeaters, n.d.)

  • Offloading and electrical work still remain (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

2. Does the SaunaLife G6 include a heater? No. The heater is a separate purchase and must be matched to the cabin and your electrical service.

  • Sold separately by retailers (SaunaHeaters, n.d.)

  • Installation should be handled by a certified electrician (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Sizing must account for cabin volume, glass area, and available capacity (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

3. How many people fit in the G6? It is commonly marketed as a five-person sauna, though official materials also mention up to six bathers.

  • Retail listings emphasize five (GoOutdoorDirect, 2025)

  • The official page references up to six bathers (SaunaLife, 2025)

  • Two-tier benches mean real comfort depends on layout and body size (SaunaMarketplace, 2026)

4. What are the G6's exterior dimensions? A retailer lists roughly 83 in. D × 95 in. W × 96 in. H, with interior dimensions near 71.5 × 80 × 80.25 in.

  • Exterior and interior figures per retailer specification table (SaunaHeaters, n.d.)

  • Published measurements vary slightly between sellers (TheSaunaHeater, 2023)

  • Confirm the current manufacturer drawing before building a pad

5. How heavy is the G6? The manual lists 2,645 lbs for the cabin and 2,976 lbs boxed.

  • Manual figures are the primary reference (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • One retailer lists a 2,756 lb shipping weight (SaunaHeaters, n.d.)

  • Plan on heavy-equipment handling either way (SaunaHeaters, n.d.)

6. What electrical service does the G6 require? It uses two separate systems: 240 V for the heater side and 120 V for lighting.

  • 240 VAC cabinet for heater control and ventilator (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • 120 VAC cabinet for lights, up to 1 kW / 9 A (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Heater-side wiring supports up to 11 kW / 46 A (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • A certified electrician must complete the connections (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

7. Can I install the G6 myself? You can manage site preparation, but the electrical work and offloading are not DIY tasks.

  • The manual requires a certified electrician (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Offloading generally requires a forklift or crane (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Final placement depends on delivery access and equipment (SaunaHeaters, n.d.)

8. What foundation does the G6 need? A stable, level base elevated at least three inches above the surrounding ground.

  • Minimum 3 in. above grade (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Manual examples: concrete blocks or strips over compacted gravel (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • A terrace or paved surface can work if elevation and support are met (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

9. Does delivery require a forklift or crane? Generally yes, given the crated weight.

  • Manual and retailer notes both indicate forklift or crane (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024; SaunaHeaters, n.d.)

  • Site access and conditions determine the exact equipment

  • Confirm who arranges and pays for offloading before shipment

10. Is the G6 suitable for cold climates? It is built for outdoor use with insulated construction, but cold-weather performance depends on heater selection and installation quality.

  • Materials and construction are designed for outdoor exposure (SaunaLife, 2025)

  • No source here supports a universal climate performance claim (SaunaLife, 2025)

  • Heater sizing and site prep matter most (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

11. What materials are used in the G6? A furniture-grade alder interior, painted spruce exterior, and full tempered-glass front wall.

  • Alder inside, painted spruce outside (SaunaLife, 2025)

  • Tempered glass front and clear glass door (SaunaLife, 2025)

  • Retailer listings put wall thickness near 7-1/16 in. (SaunaHeaters, n.d.)

12. Does the G6 have Bluetooth and Wi-Fi controls? Yes to Bluetooth speakers and LED lighting control; exact app functionality depends on the installed control system.

  • Bluetooth speaker setup is documented in the manual (SaunaLife Installation Manual, 2024)

  • Lighting is dimmable LED with app or remote control (SaunaLife, 2025)

  • Confirm control behavior for your specific configuration (SaunaLife, 2025)

13. What warranty applies to the G6? The manual describes a limited lifetime warranty for qualifying residential use by the original retail purchaser.

What We Still Don't Know

Honest gaps in the current documentation — worth asking your dealer about directly:

  • Heat-up time. No documented figure exists under defined starting temperature, heater output, and ambient conditions.

  • Operating cost. There is no supported cost-per-session or monthly energy figure for this model.

  • Comparative energy efficiency. Insulated construction and double glazing suggest thermal benefits, but no comparative testing against other outdoor saunas is available.

  • Approved heater list. Compatibility should be confirmed against current manufacturer documentation rather than inferred from retailer merchandising.

  • G7 specifications. Without equivalent current documentation, a G6-versus-G7 comparison would be guesswork.

  • True capacity. The five-versus-six-bather discrepancy remains unresolved between manufacturer and retail sources (SaunaLife, 2025; GoOutdoorDirect, 2025).

  • Long-term durability data. No published service-life or finish-longevity data exists for this model in varied climates.

  • Model-specific health outcomes. General sauna research does not transfer to a specific cabin, and none of the available sources support health claims for the G6.
